AZ: Source: Arizona Department of Education, ESA Quarterly Reports, FY2024 Quarter 4 (Table 7, “Number of students enrolled in ESA program by zip code”). Each quarterly report restates enrollment as of that quarter — a running level, not that quarter’s new sign-ups — so the year-end Q4 report IS the fiscal-year figure and the quarters are never added together. Arizona’s own FY2024 levels run 66,457 (Q1), 71,520 (Q2), 74,996 (Q3), 74,578 (Q4); the extracted zip table reconciles exactly to the 74,578 the Q4 report prints for itself. 74,358 of those students are mapped — 37 zip codes in the report have no matching Census ZCTA polygon (220 students). Unit is students, per the report’s own headings.
FL: Source: Florida Office of Independent Education and Parental Choice, FTC Scholarship Program Quarterly Report, June 2023.
NC: Source: North Carolina State Education Assistance Authority, Opportunity Scholarship Program report, 2024–25.
TX: Source: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, TEFA Annual Demographic Report, 2026–27. Excludes districts with fewer than 30 participants (privacy suppression) and one non-district recipient (Harris County Dept. of Education).
NH: Source: NH Department of Education, Division of Analytics and Resources, Education Freedom Account Data Fact Sheet, November 2025.
WV: Source: West Virginia Hope Scholarship Board, 2024–2025 Annual Report (county-level recipient table).
AK: Source: Alaska Dept. of Education & Early Development, Correspondence School Reporting, January 2025. District total adjusted +1 (Cordova City School District) to reconcile with the report’s own statewide total.
RI: Source: RI Division of Taxation, "Summary of Scholarships Issued" 2025 reports for 5 SGOs (FACE, ACSI, STEPS, FRIDS, StarScholars), combined by this analysis. One scholarship with an invalid zip code is excluded; one SGO subtotal (ACSI/Westbay) does not reconcile with its own row-level detail in the source document.
SCHOOLS: Source: National Center for Education Statistics, Private School Universe Survey directory (most recent available year per state). Addresses geocoded via the US Census Bureau Geocoder, with OpenStreetMap Nominatim as fallback; some locations are approximate (city/zip-level) where a street address could not be resolved.
IN: Source: Indiana Choice Scholarship Program Annual Report, Appendix H (Choice Scholarship Students by County of Residence), 2024–25 school year, Period One + Period Two combined by this analysis. Counts under 10 are asterisked in the source to comply with FERPA and are treated as 0 in this total (the report’s own statewide total is 76,067; this county-level sum is 75,930 — the ~137-student gap reflects suppressed small counts across roughly a third of counties).
AZ_FY2026: Source: Arizona Department of Education, ESA Quarterly Reports, FY2026 Quarter 3 (Table 7). FY2026 Q4 has not been published as of this writing, so this is the program’s enrollment level as of Q3 rather than a year-end figure — a partial-year snapshot, not directly comparable to the FY2024 year-end figure above. As with FY2024 this is the latest quarter’s level, not a sum of quarters (the FY2026 levels run 93,993 / 99,034 / 102,891); the zip table reconciles exactly to the 102,891 the Q3 report prints for itself. 102,211 are mapped — 62 zip codes have no matching Census ZCTA polygon (680 students).
WI: Source: Wisconsin Dept. of Public Instruction, "2025-26 School Year Student HC, FTE & Annualized Payment" summary (Private School Choice Programs: MPCP, RPCP, WPCP + Special Needs Scholarship Program), 3rd Friday September 2025 count, cross-walked against the WI State Private School Directory for addresses. Methodology: the enrollment report lists one line per school/system (e.g. "Assumption Catholic Schools - Wisconsin Rapids") without a street address, only a name and township; the directory lists individual school campuses with full addresses but no enrollment figures. Each report line was matched to the directory by name + city; where a report line named a multi-campus system with several directory campuses in the same city (e.g. Assumption High School + Assumption Middle School, both Wisconsin Rapids), that system’s enrollment was split evenly across its campuses so no students are lost and each campus appears on the map. One school (Trinity Lutheran School, West Bend) required falling back to a directory entry marked CLOSED (its most recent known address) since it has no OPEN entry as of the current directory snapshot despite reporting active enrollment. This crosswalk resolved 100% of the report’s 60,972 statewide headcount to 444 geocoded campus locations across 201 zip codes (one small zip, 45 students, has no matching Census ZCTA boundary and is excluded from the choropleth). Because this required splitting/matching logic rather than a direct 1:1 address lookup, treat individual campus-level enrollment figures as good estimates rather than exact per-campus counts; the zip-level and statewide totals are exact.
NC_SCHOOLS: Source: North Carolina Division of Non-Public Education, private school directory ("Current Open Private Schools"), January 2026 snapshot, replacing this map's earlier NCES Private School Universe Survey pull for North Carolina. 971 schools geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (864 matched) with OpenStreetMap Nominatim as fallback for the remaining 107; one school's directory-listed city field was corrupted (it duplicated the street address instead) and was geocoded to its zip code's centroid instead of a street address. This directory does not report religious affiliation, coed status, school level, or enrollment, so those fields read "Not reported" throughout — unlike the NCES-derived data used for most other states.
IN_SCHOOLS: Source: Indiana Department of Education, 2026-27 State Choice Private School Directory (PDF), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull for Indiana. 417 schools geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (391 matched) with Nominatim as fallback for the remaining 26. The source PDF's text extraction concatenated each school's street address directly against its city with no separating space (e.g. "127 N 4th StreetDecatur"); addresses were split programmatically using known street-suffix boundaries and spot-checked against a 20-school random sample (one systematic bug found and fixed: cities beginning with "South", e.g. South Bend, were being mis-split). Grade level (bucketed to Elementary/Secondary/Combined) and instructional mode (In-Person/Hybrid/Virtual) are as reported in the directory; religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not in this directory's fields.
RI_SCHOOLS: Source: Rhode Island Department of Education, RIDE-approved Nonpublic Schools directory, SY2026-27 (PDF), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull for Rhode Island. 81 schools geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (66 matched) with Nominatim as fallback for the remaining 15, including one school (The Prout School) whose row in the source PDF is missing its city/state/zip entirely; that one school's location was recovered by geocoding its street address and name directly, which resolved unambiguously to South Kingstown. The source PDF's text extraction ran each school's name directly against its administrative contact's name with no separating space (an artifact of the original document's column layout), so a number of "name" values here retain a trailing contact-name fragment; this does not affect the address/city/zip fields used to place each school, which were independently verified for all 81 schools. Religious affiliation, coed status, school level, and enrollment are not in this directory's fields.
NH_SCHOOLS: Source: NH Department of Education, "NH Nonpublic Schools by Approval Status" directory (PDF), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull for New Hampshire. This directory lists each school's town of location but no street address at all, so all 133 schools are geocoded to their town's centroid via OpenStreetMap Nominatim rather than an exact address — every school in this list is flagged as an approximate location on the map. Religious affiliation, coed status, school level, and enrollment are not in this directory's fields.
FL_SCHOOLS: Source: Florida Office of Independent Education and Parental Choice, State Private School Directory (2025-26), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull for Florida. 3,357 of 3,409 directory rows had a usable address (52 had none and were excluded); geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (2,977 matched) with Nominatim as fallback for the remainder. A handful of rows had data-entry errors in the source spreadsheet — a school's city field containing a copy of its own zip code, an email address misfiled into the street-address column, and two schools listing an out-of-state administrative address for what appear to be online/virtual programs — each was individually corrected or, where no true street address could be determined, geocoded to its zip code's centroid. Unlike the NCES data used for most other states, this directory does report religious affiliation/denomination, coed status, grade level, and per-grade enrollment, all of which are retained here; it does not classify a school "type" (Montessori, special education, etc.), so that field reads "Not reported" for every Florida school.
LA_SCHOOLS: Source: Louisiana Department of Education, 2025-26 State Private School Directory ("NonPublic Schools" sheet) — Louisiana's schools are newly added to this map with this release. Most schools (282 of 361) include the state's own latitude/longitude directly; the remainder were geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder with Nominatim as fallback, including one school whose listed street address was the literal placeholder text "TBD" and was geocoded to its city instead. Louisiana has no participation-program data loaded on this map yet, only its private-school directory. Religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not in this directory's fields; school level is bucketed from each school's reported grade configuration.
AL_SCHOOLS: Source: Alabama State Department of Education private school directory, replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 623 schools (after dropping 154 exact-duplicate rows in the source workbook); geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder with Nominatim fallback. Many rows list a P.O. Box rather than a street address (geocoded to city/zip level) and several carry a placeholder '00000' zip (treated as missing). Two Nominatim matches landed out of state ('Phenix City' -> Phoenix AZ; 'Monroeville' -> Monroeville PA) and were corrected. Grade level is from the directory's Grade Range column (absent for ~1/3 of rows); religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported.
AR_SCHOOLS: Source: Arkansas Division of Elementary and Secondary Education private school locator, replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 100 schools. The source packs the address into one newline-delimited cell, and only about half the rows have a street address or zip; because the Census geocoder resolved almost none of them, all 100 were geocoded via Nominatim - at street level where possible, otherwise at city level (the majority). Grade level is from the Grades Offered column; religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported. Enrollment is not in this directory; where a school participates in the LEARNS EFA program, its total enrollment is taken from the EFA audit report's Table 1 (flagged enroll_source "ar_efa_2024_25").
IA_SCHOOLS: Source: Iowa Department of Education, 2026-27 Iowa Nonpublic School Building Directory (Preliminary), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 256 schools, geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (236 matched) with Nominatim fallback. School level is Iowa's own classification (Elementary / K-12 / High / Middle / Preschool) mapped to this map's Elementary/Secondary/Combined buckets; religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported.
ID_SCHOOLS: Source: Idaho State Department of Education, Idaho Private Schools list (updated November 2025), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 143 of 151 rows had a usable address (8 dropped); geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (133 matched) with Nominatim fallback for the rest. Grade level is from the Grades Served column; religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported.
KS_SCHOOLS: Source: Kansas State Department of Education, Private Accredited Educational Organizations and Schools listing from the 2025-2026 Kansas Educational Directory, replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 137 schools. The source is a block-per-school layout (not a table); each block was parsed for name, county, street address, city/zip, and the ELEM/MS/JH/SH enrollment line (111 schools have a nonzero enrollment). Five schools have no city/zip line in the source and were placed from a city tag in the school name, a same-address sibling, or their county seat. School level is inferred from level keywords in each school's name; religious affiliation and coed status are not reported. Geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (123 matched) with Nominatim fallback.
KY_SCHOOLS: Source: Kentucky Department of Education, KBE Certified Non-Public Schools directory, replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 192 schools parsed from the PDF table. The street-address/city split has no delimiter in the source text and was resolved with a list of known two-word Kentucky place names (Fort Knox, Fort Campbell, Pippa Passes, Pewee Valley, Cox's Creek, etc.); grade level is from the grade-span column. Two Nominatim matches first resolved to a same-named place in another state ('Florence' and a 'Hagar Hill' typo) and were corrected. Religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported. Geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (159 matched) with Nominatim fallback.
ND_SCHOOLS: Source: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction statewide school directory, filtered to the 59 rows classified 'Nonpublic School' (the source file lists all public and nonpublic schools together), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. Physical address preferred over mailing address; grade level from the Grade Span column. Religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported. Geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (51 matched) with Nominatim fallback.
OH_SCHOOLS: Source: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce nonpublic school directory, replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 896 open nonpublic schools. The single combined mailing-address cell was split from the right (zip, state, city, then street) so commas inside a street address survive; grade level from the Grade Span column. Religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported. Geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder in ~150-row chunks (857 matched) with Nominatim fallback.
TN_SCHOOLS: Source: Tennessee Department of Education private school directory (three category sheets, combined), replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. 671 schools with a Tennessee address (rows whose listed address is out of state - several on the online-schools sheet - are excluded). Tennessee reports enrollment: PreK plus K-12 student counts are summed (628 of 671 schools have a nonzero total). Grade level from the Grade Span column; religious affiliation and coed status are not reported. Geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder in ~150-row chunks (617 matched) with Nominatim fallback.
UT_SCHOOLS: Source: Utah State Board of Education (USBE) Schools Directory Export, filtered to the 115 private schools, replacing this map's earlier NCES pull. The Grades column had been silently reinterpreted as dates by Excel (e.g. a '9-12' range stored as 2026-09-12) and was recovered as month=low-grade, day=high-grade before bucketing to Elementary/Secondary/Combined. Religious affiliation, coed status, and enrollment are not reported. Geocoded via the Census Bureau's batch geocoder (97 matched) with Nominatim fallback for the rest, including several P.O. boxes placed at city/zip level.
SEATS: Enrollment (“seats”) methodology: where a state's own directory reports enrollment (Florida, Tennessee, Kansas, Wisconsin) that figure is used as-is. For all other schools, enrollment is borrowed from the school's matching record in the NCES Private School Universe Survey (PSS), 2023-24 vintage, matched by school name + city (with conservative token-overlap fallbacks). These NCES-sourced seats are an access proxy, not a current-year count, and are flagged per school as “NCES 2023-24” in the tooltip. About 15% of schools match no PSS record (newer than the 2023-24 snapshot or not surveyed) and carry no seat figure, so seats-based totals undercount in those areas. When a newer PSS release is published, the same crosswalk is re-run against it.
ACS: Per-child denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024 5-year, table B14003 (school enrollment by type, age, and sex), pulled at ZCTA, county, and unified-school-district geography to match each program's reporting unit. “School-age population” is ages 5-17 (public + private + not-enrolled), a close proxy for K-12; “ACS private-school attendance” is the same table's private-school count for those ages. ACS 5-year figures are estimates with margins of error that widen for small areas. Access is joined to each choropleth area by ZIP/ZCTA code or county/district name (~99%+ matched; a few same-named Texas districts can't be disambiguated by name and contribute no population, shown as the population-coverage figure). The access Gini is population-weighted (seats per child across where children actually live).
MD: Source: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of Accountability, BOOST (Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today) Scholarship Program, Joint Chairman's Report FY2025-26 (January 2026), table “Scholarships Awarded and Accepted by Applicant County of Residence” (pp. 36-37). Counts are BOOST scholarships awarded AND accepted, mapped by the applicant's county of residence (where participating families live), not the school's location. Statewide: 2,796 students / $9,505,154 across 23 jurisdictions; Kent County reported none and is shown as 0. Private-school locations for Maryland come from the NCES directory (see MD_SCHOOLS), which enables the supply-side (seats/access) and BOOST participating-school analysis shown in the panel.
MD_SCHOOLS: Source: NCES Private School Universe Survey directory for Maryland (535 schools), geocoded via the US Census Bureau batch geocoder (496 matched) with OpenStreetMap Nominatim as fallback for the remaining 39; 8 schools resolved only to city/zip level. Schools that enroll BOOST scholarship students are flagged from the program's own by-school table (Joint Chairman's Report FY2025-26, “Scholarships Awarded and Accepted by School County Location and School Name,” pp. 9-22), which lists 152 participating schools enrolling 2,796 students totaling $9,505,154; 125 were matched to a school in this NCES directory by name within county, and the rest — several newer than or absent from the NCES snapshot — are counted in the aggregate BOOST metrics but not shown on an individual school dot.
MO: Source: MOScholars (Missouri Empowerment Scholarship Accounts) participation from “MOScholars Students by Geography” (PRiME Center at Saint Louis University for the Missouri State Treasurer’s Office, June 2026), Table A.1 — participating students by home public school district, SY2026-27 (the most recent of three years shown). Each district is joined to its Census unified-school-district polygon by NCES id (= shapefile GEOID): 11,598 students across 288 districts. Two caveats: the report suppresses any district count below 5 (“< 5”), treated here as 0, which affects 136 districts and makes the mapped total a floor; and 29 small elementary districts (70 students) have no polygon in the unified-school-district shapefile and are not mapped. The companion “MO Scholars Private Schools” report lists the private schools that received MOScholars funds in SY2025-26 (287 schools, $38,353,502.80 total); 184 were matched to a school in the NCES directory by name (disambiguated by city where a name was shared); a further 34 that aren’t in the directory were placed by an OpenStreetMap Nominatim name+city lookup (validated to fall near the claimed city, so shared parish names aren’t mismatched across metros) and shown as approximate scholarship-only dots. That is 218 of the 287 funded schools mapped; the remaining 69 (no reliable geocode) are counted in Missouri’s aggregate scholarship metrics but not shown on an individual dot.
AR: Source: Arkansas LEARNS Education Freedom Account (EFA) audit report, 2024-25, “Table 1: Participating Private Schools” (pp. 12-16): 126 private schools enrolled 10,834 EFA students (about 43% of those schools' 25,110 total seats). Because the report is BY SCHOOL, not by geography (like Wisconsin), the heat-map is built by crosswalking each school to the Arkansas private-school directory for its location and aggregating EFA students by the COUNTY THE SCHOOL IS IN — this is the private schools' location, NOT where participating families live. 81 of the 126 schools matched the directory by name (with city disambiguation and a conservative distinctive-word rule); 7 more that aren't in the 100-school directory were geocoded by name+city via Nominatim and validated to Arkansas. That places 88 schools / 9,380 of the 10,834 EFA students (87%) on the map across 26 counties; the remaining ~13% could not be located and are counted in Arkansas's aggregate EFA metrics but not shown. County (not ZIP) geography is used because only ~half the directory rows carry a street or ZIP, so a city-level geocode reliably identifies the county but not the ZIP — see AR_SCHOOLS.
